topic: Proposed NFSA Amendment for AAY Households

subtopics.title: NFSA 2013 and Beneficiary Categories
subtopics.summary: The National Food Security Act 2013 was enacted to ensure food and nutritional security through subsidised foodgrains under the Targeted Public Distribution System. It made foodgrain access a legal right for two-thirds of the population. AAY households get 35 kg per month and PHH households get 5 kg per person per month at subsidised rates.
facts: NFSA 2013 was enacted to ensure food and nutritional security
It provides subsidised foodgrains through the Targeted Public Distribution System
It made foodgrain access a legal right for two-thirds of the population
AAY is meant for the poorest of the poor households
AAY families get 35 kg per month, fixed per household
PHH get 5 kg per person per month
AAY entitlement is fixed per household; PHH entitlement is per person

subtopics.title: PDS Background and PMGKAY
subtopics.summary: The Public Distribution System was introduced by the British during World War II, after the 1942-43 Bengal famine, to control food prices and ration foodgrains. It was initially focused on urban food security and expanded to tribal and poor areas after the Green Revolution. PMGKAY (2020) added extra free foodgrains for NFSA beneficiaries.
facts: PDS in India was introduced by the British during World War II
It was introduced after the 1942-43 Bengal famine to control food prices and ration foodgrains
Initially focused on urban food security
Expanded to tribal and poor areas after the Green Revolution in the 1970s and 1980s
Essential goods distributed: wheat, sugar, rice and kerosene
Administered by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
RPDS (1992) aims to extend PDS access to remote, hilly areas through an area-based approach
PMGKAY (2020) provided an extra 5 kg of free foodgrains to AAY and PHH beneficiaries
PMGKAY covered 81.35 crore people alongside regular PDS entitlements
Kerala set up one of India's earliest PDS in 1962; Tamil Nadu introduced universal free rice distribution in 2011
